verification.notes: NOT VERIFIED. Sandbox run 2026-09-25 (codex-cli 0.153.4, copy of the repo with the staged hook at .codex/, project trust passed per-invocation with -c, no change to ~/.codex/config.toml): `codex exec` answered NONE and an instrumented copy of the hook never created its marker file, so the hook did not execute. Consistent with the documented requirement that a non-managed hook be approved by the user (persisted, by hash). Whether the project-trust override or the missing hook approval blocked it was not isolated. `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` exists and would probably prove delivery, but it bypasses the approval control and was deliberately not used. To verify: run Codex interactively in a project containing .codex/, trust the project, review and approve the hook, start a session, and ask the agent to quote the 'authority:' line.

limitations: Project-local hooks load only when the project .codex/ layer is trusted, and a non-managed hook needs explicit user approval (tracked by hash; a changed hook needs re-approval).
additionalContextLimit defaults to about 2500 tokens; larger output is saved to disk and only a preview is sent. The staged hook sets 5000.
Codex documents plain stdout as developer context; SessionStart exit-code and stderr behavior is not documented, so the adapter only exits 0 or 1.
Assumes the session working directory is the project root.
Adding .codex/ contradicts the current matrix rule 'Codex takes no adapter file beyond AGENTS.md'; needs a governed change.
